## Rule  (DECODED 2026-06-07 from ARC-GEN generator `task_234bbc79`)

**Snake reassembly.** The OUTPUT is a single continuous height-3 colored "snake" (one
4-connected worm spanning the full width, partitioned into 3–4 differently-colored
segments). The INPUT is that snake **cut into segments and scrambled**:
- each segment is separated from the next by **exactly one empty gap column** (+ optionally one extra empty col at the far right);
- each segment is **vertically offset** by an arbitrary in-grid amount (segment 0 offset 0);
- each segment's **two endpoint pixels are recolored gray(5)** — EXCEPT the global first and global last pixel of the whole snake, which keep their color.

To INVERT (input→output):
1. **Remove empty columns** (gap + extra removal = horizontal pack). Every segment column has ≥1 colored pixel; gaps/padding are fully empty — so "drop empty columns" is exact.
2. **Vertical realign** so the snake reconnects: per-column shift `S(c) = cumsum(delta)`, where at each segment-start column `c`, `delta = grayrow[c-2] - grayrow[c]` (the gap is exactly 1 wide, so the previous segment's last col is `c-2`). `grayrow[c]` = row of the gray pixel in column c. Joint grays land on the SAME output row (snake crosses joints horizontally).
3. **Recolor gray → segment color.** `segcolor(c)` = a single 1×3 horizontal max of the per-column real color (gray masked to 0). Leak-safe: gaps are 1-wide and the measured propagation distance for gray-only columns is exactly 1 (no segment is wholly gray — width-2 segments always turn, adding ≥1 colored interior pixel).

Generators: height always 3; `wides=[randint(2,4)]*randint(3,4)`; so **W_out = sum(wides) ∈ [6,16]** and **W_in = W_out + (nseg-1) + extra ∈ [8,20]** (both bounds generator-exact). Verified: numpy ref + ONNX = 267/267 official + thousands of fresh oracle pairs.

## Algorithm sketch
```
occ        = column has any colored pixel (ch1..9)
packed     = drop empty columns                       # gap/extra removal
delta[c]   = (grayrow[c-2]-grayrow[c]) if seg_start(c) else 0   # seg_start = occ & ~occ[c-1]
S          = cumsum(delta)                            # per-column vertical shift
out[r,c]   = segcolor(c) if snake[r-S(c), c] else bg  # realign + recolor
```

## Cost analysis (v30, cost 2278 = memory 2179 + params 99). **Full v1→v16 ladder + breakthrough writeups: `_archive/task046_history.md`.**

Three "floors" I claimed were all wrong (lesson: never trust a floor claim), then two dtype wins:
1. **Colour read (was "2160 B crop floor")** → **dual-dilated Conv** `[1,10,2,2]`, `dilations=[27,10]`, `w[0,ch,0,0]=ch` reads the FREE input and emits `[1,1,3,20]` colour index in ONE op (row taps 0/27 crop rows 30→3, col taps 0/10 crop cols 30→20, channel-sum reduces 10→1). 40 params, 240 B. See technique **#94**.
2. **Pack (was "OneHot Sel 640 B floor")** → **TopK**: `score = 100·occ − c` ranks occupied cols above unoccupied and ascending-by-column, so `TopK(k=16).indices = src(t)` directly → `Gather`. No cumsum, no select-matrix (−581). Trailing idx (t≥W′) hit `CGroll=0` cols → zeroed by `inrange`.
3. **Roll** → roll the **BOOL** snake mask (`Pad(P_b)` bool 140 vs CGorig F16 280), apply colour after via `Where(rolled_mask, segcolor, 0)` — segcolor is column-invariant so post-roll is exact; drops CGorig (−200).

4. **uint8 colour path (v15, −323)**: every colour tensor (Mh, M_nogray, segcolor, CGroll, CGpack, CGs) flows ONLY through Greater/Equal/Where/ReduceMax/MaxPool/Gather/GatherElements — all uint8-supported at opset 13, and NONE through Sub/Add/Mul — so `Cast(conv F32 → uint8)` halves them. (Realign chain stays F16: it has signed values & Sub/ReduceSum, and ORT lacks uint8/int8 Where+ReduceSum even @ opset 14.)
5. **seg-start in pure BOOL (v16, −61)**: `And(occ_b, Not(occ_prev_b))` replaces the signed `occ − occ_prev` Sub (bool tensors 1 B vs F16 2 B).

**v24 recovery reductions:** direct 3×3 segcolor MaxPool deletes `colmax`; opset20 bool `ReduceMax(P_b)` deletes the uint8 occupancy max+Greater path; pre-pack gap sentinel removes `Wp`/`inrange_b`/`CGs`; rank-1 column vectors delete the occ reshape and shrink Pad/Slice constants; pack-before-roll shrinks roll tensors from width 20 to 16; TopK scoring via `Where(occ_b, keep_scores, drop_scores)` deletes the occ Cast/Mul/Sub chain; Slice→Pad shortens left-shift helpers.

**v25 residual-index shrink (2026-06-20, −32 vs v24):** since the graph is already opset20, ORT accepts `CumSum(F16)` on `delta_pack`. v25 computes `S_h = CumSum(delta_pack)` in F16, then casts only `S_h` to INT32 for `GatherElements` indexing. This deletes v24's pre-CumSum `delta_i` INT32[16] (64 B) and adds `S_h` F16[16] (32 B), while keeping the required INT32 `S`/`gidx` index lane. Static/profile cost: 2307 = 2179 memory + 128 params.

**v30 param-side shrink (2026-06-22, −29 vs v25):** memory is unchanged at 2179; all savings are initializer element-count params. Two rank-4 Pad nodes use opset-18 axes form (`pad_rows2`: 8→2+1, final `pad_out`: 8→4+2, −7). `CumSum` reuses existing `w0=[0]` as the axis input (−1). Dropped TopK columns no longer need distinct negative scores because all dropped slots are masked to sentinel later, so `score_drop_h[20]` becomes existing scalar `zero_h` (−20). The 1D `occ_prev_b` left pad becomes `Concat(false1_b, occ_prev_raw_b)` (2→1, −1). Total params 128→99; byte-equal full.

**Residual largest (not a new floor claim):** one-hot `oh_b`[1,10,3,16] bool 480, dilated-conv `M` F32 240, packed roll `gidx` int32 192, `tk_idx` int64 128, `CGpad_b` bool 112, `S` int32 64, and `S_h` F16 32. Known rejected pushes still apply: ScatterElements pack has duplicate-index UB; sub-int32 gather indices are scorer-rejected; Conv output follows the F32 input, so the source-read plane is not narrowable without paying a full input cast.

**The 480 B `oh_b` one-hot is a HARD output-formulation floor (proven 2026-06-17, worker-046).** Active output is only 3×16, and LIVE needs ch0=True for active-region background but all-False outside the padded grid. Channel-small ordering bills `oh_b`[1,10,3,16]=480 with Pad as the free output; spatial-full ordering bills `CGfull`[1,1,30,30]=900 with Equal as the free output. Gather-BOOL/OneHot-axis-1 also bottleneck at ≥480.

- 2026-05-19: CumSum replacement (opset 11 upgrade, replace v14/v15 with CumSum): saves 800 params but each Pad op gains 8 int64 inputs (7 Pads × 8 = 56 params); net -744 params = -744B. Low ROI given the padslice already staged. _(Note: applies to the OLD pre-rebuild lineage; the 2026-06-07 v3 rewrite uses CumSum throughout and it IS the right call there — see below.)_
- 2026-06-07 [v3 rewrite, ruled out by measurement]:
  - **Conv-first instead of crop-first**: Conv(full input)→[1,1,30,30] F32 = 3600 B > Slice→[1,9,3,20] crop 2160 B. Crop-first wins; do not Conv the full 30×30.
  - **Triangular-matmul cumsum instead of CumSum op**: a [20,20] cumsum matrix = 400 params (dtype-blind element count) per cumsum × 2 = 800 cost, which exceeds the ~400 B of F16 working-tensor memory it would unlock. CumSum (param-free) is strictly better here.
  - **F16 CumSum in old low-opset probes**: the earlier INVALID_GRAPH finding applied to the old low-opset lineage. v25 re-tested the narrow route at opset20 and passed scorer + full gates by using `CumSum(F16)` only before the still-required INT32 index cast.
  - **"Colour read is crop-floored at 2160 B"** — FALSE (corrected v8-v12). A **dual-dilated valid Conv** (kernel `[1,10,2,2]`, `dilations=[27,10]`, weight `[0,ch,0,0]=ch`) reads the free `[1,10,30,30]` input and outputs `[1,1,3,20]` colour-index in ONE op (crops both spatial axes via dilated taps + sums channels), 40 params, no 2160 B multi-channel crop. **General reusable technique** — see `Onnx_Advanced/techniques.md` #94 (dilated crop+reduce) + #95 (TopK compaction). SAFE floor now ~2676 B (v16).
  - **ScatterElements pack instead of OneHot+matmul** (would save ~147 B): REJECTED. Gap/padding columns collide on occupied columns' target positions, and ONNX ScatterElements with duplicate indices is **undefined behaviour** — relying on "last write (gap, =0) loses to occupied" is a hidden-eval landmine (the eval ORT may process in a different order). The OneHot+matmul pack is order-independent and exact. Do not swap it for Scatter to save bytes.
  - **v6 no-sentinel pack is NOT UB**: it works because gap/padding cols have CGroll=0, so their OneHot rows contribute 0 to the *matmul* (sum of products), which is order-independent — distinct from the Scatter case above. Safe.
